summary.text: A son of Talaus in the Biantid house at Argos, Pronax was father of Amphithea — whom Adrastus married — and of Lycurgus, who quarrelled with Amphiaraus before the march on Thebes.

story.text: Apollodorus counts Pronax among the children Talaus begot on Lysimache, in the same breath as Adrastus, Mecisteus, Aristomachus, and Eriphyle. Of Pronax he records only that he had a son Lycurgus; of Adrastus, that he married Amphithea, daughter of Pronax — so the Argive king wed his brother's daughter and the Theban war was bound into a single kindred.

Pausanias saw the feud remembered in paint. At Delphi, Polygnotus showed Amphiaraus and Lycurgus son of Pronax coming to blows while Adrastus and Tydeus held them apart — the quarrel of the seer who foresaw disaster and the prince whose sister's marriage had tied him to the expedition.
